Three ways to fix the router band — each shown under the hero, since that is where it actually sits.
Option A — compact utility strip

Treats it as wayfinding furniture, not a section: no section padding, ~56px tall, hairline dividers so the four options read as one connected control rather than four floating links. The question sits inline and slightly heavier than the answers, separated by a rule so it can't be mistaken for a choice.

Option B — question-led split

Keeps it a real section but fixes the hierarchy: the question becomes a proper heading in the display face, and the four answers become a 2×2 ruled list opposite it. The space is now occupied rather than empty. Costs more vertical room, and reuses the two-column shape the Story section already has.

Option C — fused to the hero

Removes the floating band entirely: the options become the hero's bottom edge, on the same photo, divided into four equal targets. Someone deciding where to go does it right after reading the headline, which is where this belongs. Also drops the page from seven sections to six.

My pick — C

The band looked weird because it was a low-content element given the footprint of a major section. B fixes that by inflating the content to match the box; C fixes it by removing the box. C also puts the choice at the moment someone is actually making it, keeps the hero photo working harder, and reduces the section count — which was the original complaint. A is the safe fallback if you want the hero left alone.
